GraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale: The timing explains the whole defect: C-BUNDLE-SESSION-HISTORY-SKILL froze a script that was verified against the live pre-migration layout (inline assistant content in session_message.data, smoke run 09:25), and OpenCode ran its storage migration at ~09:51 the same day (migration table entries 20261120004954_machine-key and siblings), moving parts into session_part with assistant content=[] — between the smoke run and the independent code review that caught it (13 USER / 0 ASSISTANT reproduced with the shipped script). The fix is therefore not a quality patch to a working extractor but a storage-layout adaptation, and it must supersede the byte-identity assumption rather than quietly edit a frozen artifact: the predecessor bundle stays immutable, and this change records the supersession and replaces the md5 pin with behavior markers. Inline content still wins when non-empty so transition-era rows cannot duplicate, and session_part text is consulted only for rows whose inline extraction is empty — the same precedence the legacy+modern merge already uses. The edit/write tool-part source for changed_files follows the observed shapes: tool parts named edit and write carry state.input.path, while summary_diffs is null on post-migration sessions, so the file list otherwise disappears. The test mirrors session-graph.test.ts — the repo's established pattern for shipped Python extractors (python3-gated, synthetic SQLite schema built with bun:sqlite, execFileSync) — because the predecessor's marker-only tests could not catch a storage migration by construction. The two secondary fixes ride along because they were confirmed review findings on the same file: URI percent-encoding for --db paths with reserved characters, and making the run command's path substitution explicit.

Alternatives.Alternative: Amend the archived C-BUNDLE-SESSION-HISTORY-SKILL bundle and quietly patch the frozen script in place. Rejected: archived bundles are immutable historical evidence, and the md5 pin is referenced by the predecessor's assumptions and smoke evidence; a successor change keeps the audit trail honest.

Fix only modern_messages and defer changed_files, docs, URI, and the run command. Rejected: all five were confirmed findings on the same shipped file, and splitting them across changes would leave the PR carrying known defects.

Derive text for every session_message row from session_part unconditionally. Rejected: transition-era rows with both inline content and parts would duplicate or race; empty-inline gating preserves the merge precedence the extractor already uses for its two existing stores.

Teach changed_files to parse shell command text for file paths. Rejected: shell parts are not recorded patches; edit and write tool parts carry explicit state.input.path, which matches the section's existing meaning ("Files mentioned by recorded patches").

DeferredDecisions.Decision: Whether the vv-reflect session-graph.py extractor needs the same session_part adaptation is deferred; the same storage gap was observed there, and it should be specified separately after this change lands.
Whether user-row text also moves to session_part in a future host generation, requiring a symmetric join, is deferred; the current generation keeps user text inline (verified 2026-11-25).

Whether the workflow plugin's review-round registration needs a fix (four review rounds in this session ended in-flight because reviewer verdicts placed the result header after prose, and in-flight rounds cannot be cancelled or followed up) is deferred; it is reported to the maintainer, not fixed here.

Scenarios.Scenario: A user asks for a recap on the current host after the 2026-11-25 migration: the extractor lists post-migration sessions, joins their session_part text parts for assistant rows with empty content, and the recap contains the assistant reports the rules prefer, with reasoning and tool transcripts still excluded.

A host still on the pre-migration V2 layout or the mixed V1+V2 layout: inline content and legacy tables produce exactly the predecessor's output; session_part is absent or empty and the new code paths are inert.

A session edited files after the migration: its edit and write tool parts contribute input paths inside the project root to the "Files mentioned by recorded patches" section, while read-only tools contribute nothing.
The extractor runs with --db pointing at a path containing a reserved character: the percent-encoded URI opens the database instead of failing with "unable to open database file".
CI without python3 on PATH: the synthetic-schema extractor test is skipped, and the delivery suites still run; nothing else degrades.
